word-counter.title: Word counter
word-counter.desc: Count words, characters, sentences and paragraphs in any text, with an estimated reading time. Nothing leaves your browser.
word-counter.lede: Paste or type any text and get an instant count of words, characters, sentences and paragraphs, plus an estimated reading time. The text stays in your browser.
word-counter.how: The text box is split on whitespace to count words, then scanned for sentence-ending punctuation and blank lines to count sentences and paragraphs. Characters are counted twice: once exactly as typed, and once with spaces removed. Reading time is the word count divided by about 200 words per minute, a rough average for prose — treat it as an estimate, not a measurement.
word-counter.example: The sentence “Send the invoice on Friday.” has 5 words, 33 characters including the space after “the”, 31 without spaces, 1 sentence and 1 paragraph. At 200 words per minute it reads in under a second.

faq.q: Is my text uploaded anywhere?
faq.a: No. Counting happens in your browser with JavaScript. The text box is never sent to a server, and nothing is stored.

faq.q: How exactly is a word counted?
faq.a: A word is any run of characters separated by whitespace. “well-known” and “don’t” each count as one word; punctuation attached to a word is counted with it.

faq.q: Why might the sentence count look wrong?
faq.a: Sentences are counted by splitting on . ! ? and similar marks. Abbreviations such as “e.g.” or decimals such as “3.5” can be counted as sentence ends, so treat the figure as an estimate.

faq.q: What does reading time assume?
faq.a: It divides the word count by 200 words per minute. Technical, dense or second-language reading is slower; skimming is faster. It is a guide, not a guarantee.

faq.q: Does it work for Arabic or Chinese?
faq.a: For languages written with spaces, yes. For Chinese and Japanese, which do not use spaces, the character count is the more useful figure. The character count is always shown.

qr-code-generator.title: QR code generator
qr-code-generator.desc: Create a QR code for a link, text or any message. Generated in your browser, downloadable as a PNG.
qr-code-generator.lede: Type a link or any short text and get a QR code you can download as a PNG. The code is drawn by your browser — the content is never sent anywhere.
qr-code-generator.how: Your text is encoded into a QR symbol: the characters become a numeric value, which is laid out on a square grid with error-correction data added so the code still scans if part of it is damaged or dirty. Larger inputs need more grid cells, so the code gets denser. The image is drawn on a canvas in your browser and exported as a PNG.
qr-code-generator.example: A link such as “https://example.com/menu” produces a compact code that scans from a few centimetres away. A 400-character Wi-Fi configuration produces a denser grid that needs to be printed larger to scan reliably.

faq.q: Is the content sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. Encoding and drawing both happen in your browser. Nothing you type is transmitted or stored.

faq.q: What can I put in a QR code?
faq.a: A website link, plain text, an email address, a phone number, or connection details for a Wi-Fi network. Links are the most reliable because phones open them directly.

faq.q: Why is my code hard to scan?
faq.a: Usually it is too small for the amount of data, or it lacks quiet space around it. Print it larger, keep a clear margin on all four sides, and make sure it is printed in high contrast on a plain background.

faq.q: Is there a length limit?
faq.a: Yes. The largest QR version holds about 2,900 bytes of ordinary text. Past that the tool reports an error instead of drawing a code that would not scan.

faq.q: Does the colour or shape matter?
faq.a: This tool draws the standard black-on-white code, which every reader supports. Extreme colours or rounded modules may look better but reduce how reliably phones scan them.

ui.label: Text or link
ui.empty: Type a link or some text first.
ui.tooLong: That is too much text for one QR code (limit is about 2,900 bytes). Shorten it and try again.

password-generator.title: Password generator
password-generator.desc: Generate a strong random password in your browser, with length and character controls and a live strength estimate.
password-generator.lede: Choose a length and which character sets to use, and generate a random password. It is built from your browser's random number generator and never leaves the page.
password-generator.how: Each character is drawn uniformly at random from the alphabet you enable, using the browser's cryptographically secure random source. Strength is shown as entropy in bits: length multiplied by the log₂ of the alphabet size. Eight bits roughly means one chance in 256 of guessing, so 60 bits and above is strong for everyday accounts and 100 bits and above is strong even against patient, well-resourced guessing.
password-generator.example: 16 characters drawn from upper case, lower case, digits and symbols gives an alphabet of 94 characters: 16 × log₂(94) ≈ 105 bits. Reducing it to 8 characters drops the same alphabet to about 52 bits — half the strength, and much easier to guess by brute force.

faq.q: Where do these passwords come from?
faq.a: From your browser's cryptographic random generator (crypto.getRandomValues). Nothing is requested from a server, so no third party sees the password.

faq.q: How strong is strong enough?
faq.a: As a rough guide, 40 bits is weak, 60–80 bits is good for most accounts, and 100 bits or more resists serious offline guessing. The tool shows the bits it calculated for your settings.

faq.q: Should I use a different password everywhere?
faq.a: Yes. Reusing a password means one breached site exposes every other account. Store unique passwords in a password manager rather than memorising them.

faq.q: Why is the password not remembered after I refresh?
faq.a: Deliberately. Nothing is stored in cookies, local storage or on a server, so a refresh simply generates a new one. Save it where you keep your other passwords.

faq.q: Can it make memorable passphrases instead?
faq.a: Not yet. This tool produces random character strings. A passphrase of random words is also a good choice, but this page does not generate one.

ui.empty: Turn on at least one character set.
ui.note: Generated locally. Nothing is stored or sent anywhere.

image-compressor.title: Image compressor
image-compressor.desc: Compress a JPG, PNG or WebP image in your browser. See the size before and after, and download the result.
image-compressor.lede: Choose an image, set the quality, and see exactly how much smaller the result is. The picture is processed inside your browser and never uploaded.
image-compressor.how: The file is decoded into pixels by your browser, then re-encoded at the quality you choose. JPEG and WebP are lossy formats, so lower quality means fewer bits and a smaller file, with visible detail loss below a certain point. PNG is lossless, so re-encoding it can only shrink the file if the image has fewer colours than before — otherwise the result can be larger, and the tool says so.
image-compressor.example: A 3.2 MB photo set to 75% JPEG quality may come back near 400 KB — about an eighth of the size, with the difference mostly invisible at normal screen size. The same file saved as lossless PNG would be far larger, not smaller, which is why the tool reports the real numbers rather than promising a percentage.

faq.q: Is my picture uploaded?
faq.a: No. Decoding, re-encoding and download all happen in your browser. The file never leaves your device.

faq.q: Which quality should I pick?
faq.a: Around 80% is a good default for photos. Use 60–70% when file size matters more than fine detail, and 90%+ when the image will be printed or cropped.

faq.q: Why did my PNG get bigger?
faq.a: PNG is lossless: the re-encoder keeps every bit of detail, and if your browser's encoder is less efficient than the original, the file grows. The tool reports the real size, and you can choose JPEG instead.

faq.q: Which format should I use?
faq.a: JPEG or WebP for photographs and anything with gradients. PNG for screenshots, logos and transparency. WebP is usually smallest but is not accepted everywhere.

faq.q: Why does it struggle with very large files?
faq.a: The image has to be held as raw pixels in memory, so a very large photo can take a while or fail on a phone. The tool shows progress and reports a clear error instead of freezing the tab.

ui.bigger: larger than the original — try JPEG quality instead
ui.failed: This image could not be decoded in your browser. Try a JPG, PNG or WebP file.

image-resizer.title: Image resizer
image-resizer.desc: Resize a picture to an exact width and height in your browser, with aspect ratio locked and a download of the result.
image-resizer.lede: Set the width or height you need, keep the aspect ratio locked, and download the resized image. The file is handled entirely inside your browser.
image-resizer.how: Your browser decodes the file into pixels, then draws those pixels onto a canvas of the size you asked for. When shrinking, the tool samples the image down; when growing, it simply makes each pixel bigger, which softens detail — no tool can invent detail that was never in the file. The result is encoded as JPEG, PNG or WebP, matching the input unless you choose otherwise.
image-resizer.example: A 4032 × 3024 phone photo resized to 1200 px wide comes out at 1200 × 900 with the ratio preserved, and is usually a few hundred kilobytes instead of several megabytes. Resizing that same photo up to 4000 px would produce a large file with no extra detail.

faq.q: Is my photo uploaded?
faq.a: No. Decoding, resizing and download happen on your device only. Nothing is sent to a server.

faq.q: Does upscaling ruin quality?
faq.a: It does not add detail. Small increases are usually fine; enlarging far beyond the original makes the image soft and blocky, because the software is guessing the in-between pixels.

faq.q: Why does the height change when I type a width?
faq.a: The aspect ratio lock keeps the picture undistorted. Unlock it only if you deliberately want to stretch or squash the image.

faq.q: Which format should I download?
faq.a: JPEG for photographs, PNG for screenshots and transparency, WebP for the smallest files where it is supported. The tool keeps your original format unless you change it.

faq.q: What if the result is bigger than the original?
faq.a: Enlarging adds pixels, and sometimes a re-encoded file grows slightly. The tool shows the real size after resizing so you can decide before downloading.

ui.badSize: Enter a width and height between 1 and 10000 pixels.
ui.failed: This image could not be decoded in your browser. Try a JPG, PNG or WebP file.

merge-pdf.title: Merge PDF files
merge-pdf.desc: Combine several PDFs into one document, in the order you choose. The files stay on your device.
merge-pdf.lede: Add two or more PDF files, put them in the order you want, and download the combined document. The files are read and written in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
merge-pdf.how: Each file is parsed in the browser and its pages are copied into a new document you control the order of. Pages keep their original size, rotation and content; only the container changes. The work runs in steps with a progress bar, because assembling a large document in one go can stall a slow device.
merge-pdf.example: Three files — cover.pdf (1 page), prices.pdf (3 pages) and terms.pdf (2 pages) — combine into a 6-page document in the order you list them. Moving prices.pdf below terms.pdf changes the output to 1, 2, 3, 4 pages without reopening either file.

faq.q: Are my PDFs uploaded?
faq.a: No. The files are read with JavaScript inside your browser and the result is written locally. Nothing is transmitted, and there is no server to receive it.

faq.q: Can I change the order of the files?
faq.a: Yes. Each file in the list can be moved up or down, or removed, before you merge. The output follows the order shown on screen.

faq.q: Why did the merge fail?
faq.a: Password-protected PDFs cannot be opened, and a very large set of files can exceed the memory your browser allows. The tool reports which file failed instead of producing a broken document.

faq.q: Will the quality or page sizes change?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied as they are, so dimensions, images and text stay exactly as they were in the source files.

faq.q: Is there a file size limit?
faq.a: There is no fixed limit — it depends on your device's memory. If a merge fails on very large files, split the job into smaller batches.

ui.empty: Add at least two PDF files.
ui.oneOnly: Add at least two files to merge — a single file needs no merging.
ui.failed: One of these files could not be opened. Password-protected or damaged PDFs fail; remove that file and try again.
ui.privacy: Files are read and written on your device only. Nothing is uploaded.

age-calculator.title: Age calculator
age-calculator.desc: Work out an exact age in years, months and days from a date of birth, with the total number of days between the two dates.
age-calculator.lede: Enter a date of birth and see the exact age in years, months and days, plus the total days between that date and today. Everything is calculated in your browser.
age-calculator.how: The calculator subtracts the calendar dates rather than the raw timestamps, so a birthday at 11pm does not lose a day. It walks year by year, then month by month, then counts the remaining days — the same method that handles February in a leap year correctly. The total-days figure counts whole days between the two dates, ignoring the time of day.
age-calculator.example: Born 5 March 2000, checked on 28 October 2026: 26 years, 7 months and 23 days — about 9,733 days in total. The year count only increases once the anniversary has passed, so it stays 26 for the whole month of March until the 5th.

faq.q: Does it handle leap years?
faq.a: Yes. Because it works on calendar dates rather than a fixed number of days per year, 29 February birthdays are counted correctly, including people born on a day that does not exist in common years.

faq.q: What if the date is in the future?
faq.a: The tool refuses it and asks for a date on or before today, instead of showing a negative age.

faq.q: Why does the age differ from my birthday on Facebook?
faq.a: Some services count a full year only after the whole birth month has passed, or use the time zone the account was created in. This tool counts exact calendar years, months and days.

faq.q: Is the total number of days exact?
faq.a: It counts whole days between the two dates, so it is exact for dates but does not include the hour of birth. Treat it as a day-level figure.

faq.q: Can I use this officially?
faq.a: For passports, legal documents or benefits, use the date printed on your official documents. This tool is a quick check, not a legal record.

ui.future: That date is in the future. Enter a date on or before today.
ui.afterAsOf: The date of birth must come before the age-on date.

percentage-calculator.title: Percentage calculator
percentage-calculator.desc: Find a percentage of a number, work out what percent one number is of another, and add or subtract a percentage — with the working shown.
percentage-calculator.lede: Three common percentage problems in one page: percentage of a number, one number as a percentage of another, and increase or decrease by a percentage. Each answer shows the working.
percentage-calculator.how: Percentage of a number multiplies the value by the percentage and divides by 100. “X is what percent of Y” divides X by Y and multiplies by 100, and is refused when Y is zero because division by zero has no answer. Increase and decrease apply the percentage to the original value first, then add or subtract it, so a 20% increase followed by a 20% decrease lands 4% below where you started — the two percentages do not cancel each other out.
percentage-calculator.example: 15% of 240 = 0.15 × 240 = 36. The number 36 is 15% of 240. Increasing 240 by 15% gives 276; decreasing 276 by 15% gives 234.60 — not back at 240, which is the trap this page shows in full.

faq.q: Why can't I divide by zero?
faq.a: Because there is no number that multiplied by zero gives a nonzero value. When the base is zero the tool says so instead of showing infinity or an error.

faq.q: What is the difference between the three modes?
faq.a: “% of” gives a part of a number. “X is what %” compares two numbers as a percentage. “Increase/decrease” applies a percentage change to a starting value.

faq.q: Are the results rounded?
faq.a: The exact result is shown to two decimal places, and the working above each answer shows the unrounded value so you can round the way you need.

faq.q: Does a 50% increase and a 50% decrease cancel out?
faq.a: No. Going up 50% and then down 50% from the new, larger number lands you 25% below where you started. The examples on this page show why.

faq.q: Is anything stored?
faq.a: No. Every calculation is done in your browser and disappears when you clear the fields or close the page.

ui.modeLabel: What do you want to find?
ui.mode2: X is what percent of Y?
ui.mode3: Increase or decrease a number by X%
ui.zeroBase: The second number cannot be zero — nothing is a percentage of zero.
ui.negPercent: Enter a percentage of 0 or more.

unit-converter.title: Unit converter
unit-converter.desc: Convert length, mass, volume, temperature and speed between metric and imperial units, with the exact factor shown.
unit-converter.lede: Pick a category, choose the units, and type a value. The conversion runs in your browser and shows the exact factor it used.
unit-converter.how: Every conversion in a category is expressed against one base unit — metres for length, kilograms for mass — using exact, defined factors such as 1 inch = 25.4 mm. The value is converted to the base unit and then to the target unit, so any pair of units can be related through the same reference. Temperature is different: it uses formulas with an offset (°F = °C × 9/5 + 32) because the scales do not start at the same point, and Kelvin starts at absolute zero.
unit-converter.example: 10 kilometres is 10,000 metres, which is 6.2137 miles. Converting 25 °C uses the offset formula: 25 × 9/5 + 32 = 77 °F. Converting 0 °C gives 32 °F, not 0 — which is exactly why temperature cannot use a simple multiplier.

faq.q: Are the conversion factors exact?
faq.a: Metric factors are exact by definition (1 inch is exactly 25.4 mm, 1 pound is exactly 0.45359237 kg). The displayed result is rounded, but the calculation uses the full value.

faq.q: Why is temperature handled differently?
faq.a: Temperature scales have different zero points, so converting needs an offset as well as a multiplier. The tool uses the standard formulas rather than a ratio.

faq.q: Which units are supported?
faq.a: Length, mass, volume, temperature and speed, covering the metric units and the common imperial and US units. More categories can be added later.

faq.q: Why does the result show so many decimals?
faq.a: It shows the exact converted value rounded to a sensible number of digits, with the full precision used in the calculation shown in the working line below.

faq.q: Does it work offline?
faq.a: Yes. Nothing needs the network: the factors are built into the page and the calculation happens in your browser.

ui.badValue: Enter a valid number, for example 12.5.
ui.kelvinNegative: Kelvin cannot be below absolute zero (0 K, −273.15 °C).

json-formatter.title: JSON formatter
json-formatter.desc: Format, minify and validate JSON in your browser, with a clear error message when the syntax is wrong.
json-formatter.lede: Paste JSON to format it with indentation, minify it to save space, or check that it is valid. The data is processed in your browser and never sent anywhere.
json-formatter.how: The input is parsed with the browser's own JSON parser, which is the same standard every language implements. Formatting re-serialises the parsed value with a chosen indentation; minifying does the same with no whitespace. Because parsing happens first, a syntax error is reported before anything is printed — with the position in the text where the parser stopped.
json-formatter.example: The compact string {"a":1,"b":[true,null,"x"]} formats across four lines with two-space indentation, showing that b is an array of three items. Minifying it again returns byte-for-byte the same compact text, since whitespace outside strings carries no meaning.

faq.q: Is my JSON sent anywhere?
faq.a: No. Parsing, formatting and validation all happen in your browser tab. Nothing is transmitted or stored.

faq.q: What is the difference between format and minify?
faq.a: Formatting adds indentation and line breaks so the structure is readable. Minifying removes every optional whitespace to make the smallest possible version. Neither changes the data.

faq.q: Why does my JSON fail to parse?
faq.a: The usual causes are a trailing comma after the last item, single quotes instead of double quotes, or an unquoted key. The message tells you where the parser stopped so you can jump straight to it.

faq.q: Does it check my data against a schema?
faq.a: No. It checks syntax only — that the text is valid JSON. Whether the structure matches what your program expects is a separate check.

faq.q: Is there a size limit?
faq.a: There is no fixed limit, but very large documents take time and memory to parse. If nothing appears after a moment, the document is probably too big for this page — split it up.
